answer: To control pink bollworm in cotton, you can use insecticides like Carbaryl 5 D, Phosalone 4 D, Profenofos 50% EC, or Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC at recommended doses. Additionally, pheromone traps can help monitor adult moth activity.
For boll rot in cotton caused by fungal pathogens like Fusarium moniliforme, Colletotrichum capsici, and others, the recommended fungicides are Copper oxychloride, Carbendazim, or Mancozeb.

To control rhinoceros beetle in coconut, maintain good sanitation by removing and burning dead trees and destroying beetle bio-stages from manure pits.
To manage red palm weevil in your coconut garden, remove and burn all wilting or damaged palms and avoid injuries on stems of palms. Fill all holes in the stem with cement.
The planting season for coconut is June-July and December-January. The recommended spacing is 25' x 25' (7.5 x 7.5 m).
To control rhizome rot in turmeric, treat seed rhizomes with copper oxychloride @ 0.3% for 30 minutes or drench with 1% Bordeaux mixture or copper oxychloride @ 0.25%.
For leaf blotch and leaf spot in turmeric, you can use Mancozeb 0.25% or copper oxy chloride 0.25%.
Applying FYM enriches the soil with organic matter, which is beneficial for turmeric growth.
For turmeric cultivation, the recommended bed spacing is 45 cm x 20 cm.
Your tomato plants showing wilting with yellow lower leaves could be suffering from Fusarium wilt caused by Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. lycopersici.
Early blight in tomato is recognised by brown spots with concentric rings in a bull's eye pattern with a yellow margin.
Early blight in turmeric can be managed by spraying mancozeb 0.2% or copper oxychloride 0.25% or propiconazole 0.1% at fortnight intervals.
